skill.name: study-first
skill.description: Load BEFORE answering any message that asks for more than a single fact, and whenever answering means reading something (a document, PDF, chat transcript, web page, code, screenshot, task status, ad campaign). It makes the agent break down EVERYTHING the user asked (including messy dictated voice messages and "scratch that" corrections), read the sources IN FULL (not the title, not the first lines, not the "succeeded" label), cross-check with a second source, and answer point by point with evidence, never writing a detail it did not actually see. Triggers on "study this", "look into it properly", "read it carefully", "analyze", "investigate", "what does it say", "how is it going", "did it work", long or dictated messages, and in Spanish "estudia", "revisa a fondo", "a profundidad", "léelo bien", "analiza", "cómo vas", "qué pasó con", "funcionó".
skill.summary: Structure complex requests, read relevant sources fully, and cross-check conclusions before giving evidence-based answers.
skill.author: rabbitdesigns22

content.user_title: Verify Sources Before Answering Complex Requests
content.value_statement: Complex requests can produce incomplete answers when sources are skimmed or status labels are trusted. Study-first guides source reading, cross-checking, and evidence-based responses.
actual_capabilities: Guides decomposition of complex messages into questions, instructions, conditions, and corrections.
Maps each request to relevant documents, prior decisions, logs, or live sources.
Directs complete reading of relevant documents and contextual review of repeated topic mentions.
Requires checking underlying logs and results instead of relying on status labels.
Calls for two agreeing signals before important conclusions and resolution of conflicting evidence.
Structures point-by-point answers with evidence, reading coverage, and explicit verification gaps.
limitations: Provides instructions only; it includes no executable scripts or dedicated source connectors.
Source access depends on the host assistant, available tools, and user permissions.
Full reading and cross-checking can increase time and context use for large sources.
Cannot guarantee accurate conclusions or independent corroboration when evidence is missing.

use_cases.title: Verify Operational Status
use_cases.description: Compare a reported task status with its logs and delivered result before reporting whether it worked.

use_cases.title: Review Format Changes
use_cases.description: Identify code that reads a data format before proposing changes and report conclusions with source evidence.

use_cases.title: Resolve Complex Client Requests
use_cases.description: Separate questions and corrections in a long message, review relevant records, and answer each request with supporting evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Read [document] fully and answer [question]. State your reading coverage, cite supporting passages, and identify anything you could not verify.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: answer a focused question from an accessible document.

prompt_templates.title: Unpack a Complex Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Break [message] into every question, condition, and correction. Use the latest corrections, inspect [sources], and answer each request with evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: handle a long or dictated message.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Reported Success
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate whether [task] worked. Compare [status], [log], and [result]. Resolve contradictions and separate verified outcomes from unknowns.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a Format Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Before changing [format], locate its readers and consumers in [project]. Cross-check compatibility evidence and report affected components, uncertainties, and recommended next steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: investigate dependencies before a code or format change.

output_examples.input: Illustrative scenario: a task dashboard says succeeded, but the supplied log ends at a permission prompt and no output is available.
output: The dashboard reports success, but the supplied log stops at a permission prompt.
The missing output prevents confirmation of the intended result.
Reading coverage: the supplied status and log were reviewed in full.

output_examples.input: Illustrative scenario: a client first requests Friday, then changes the deadline to Monday. The supplied brief confirms Monday but omits the price.
output: The current requested deadline is Monday.
The latest client correction and the brief agree on Monday.
The price remains unverified because neither supplied source states it.
Reading coverage: the supplied message and brief were reviewed in full.

best_practices: Provide the original sources and keep access limited to material relevant to the request.
Supply corroborating evidence for important conclusions, especially when money, publication, or deletion is involved.
Require explicit reading coverage and preserve uncertainty when sources are missing or contradictory.
anti_patterns: Treating a success label, filename, or redirect as proof of the underlying result.
Filling missing names, commands, causes, or numbers with plausible guesses.
Ignoring later corrections or leaving questions in a long request unanswered.

faq.question: What does study-first provide?
faq.answer: It provides a workflow for decomposing requests, reading relevant sources, cross-checking conclusions, and answering with evidence.

faq.question: Does every question require the full workflow?
faq.answer: No. For a single fact from one source, it directs the assistant to check that source and answer.

faq.question: Does it install tools or run scripts?
faq.answer: No. The skill contains written instructions only. Any source inspection depends on tools already available to the assistant.

faq.question: How does it handle missing sources?
faq.answer: It directs the assistant to identify unread material, explain access gaps, and separate verified information from unverified claims.

faq.question: Can it guarantee correct answers?
faq.answer: No. Its checks can reduce unsupported claims, but results still depend on source quality, available access, and assistant execution.

faq.question: Are the linked companion skills required?
faq.answer: No required installation is stated. The document presents one-answer and never-twice as complementary skills.
